job.text:
Senior Product Manager, Model Evaluation
Halcyon AI — New York, NY (hybrid, 2 days/week) or remote in US Eastern

Halcyon builds the evaluation layer enterprise teams use to keep LLM deployments reliable. We're hiring a senior PM to own the evaluation product line end to end.

What you'll own
- The roadmap for offline eval runs, regression detection, and human review workflows
- Defining what "quality" means in the product, with our applied research group
- Weekly contact with customers running evals in production

Who you'll work with
You'll report to the VP of Product and work with a dedicated pod of 9 engineers and 2 designers.

What we're looking for
- 4+ years in product management, including developer or infrastructure products
- Hands-on LLM application experience
- Comfort defining an ambiguous problem space and taking it to GA

Compensation
- Base: $190,000 - $235,000
- Equity, full benefits, 22 days PTO. No on-call rotation for product.

(Fictional company, written for this demo.)

reasoning: This posting matches the target profile almost line for line: senior PM on AI evaluation infrastructure, a dedicated engineering pod, clearly scoped ownership, NYC hybrid or Eastern remote, and a disclosed band. No preference is seriously threatened. The shipped JPMorgan evaluation framework is unusually direct evidence for this exact product line, which makes the candidate a strong applicant rather than a marginal one.

Dedicated pod of 9 engineers and 2 designers — no substituting for an engineering team
Disclosed compensation band and no on-call, both stated up front
NYC hybrid or Eastern remote, no relocation question to resolve
concerns: The posting says "4+ years PM" and the candidate is at roughly four — at the floor rather than comfortably above it
Company stage was not stated in the posting; resolved by research below
Reporting into a VP of Product means the Director path depends on how the team grows
research_summary: Two searches. The first established that Halcyon AI is a Series B evaluation-tooling company; the second confirmed the NYC office and an active remote-hiring policy for Eastern-time candidates.

# Sofia Tofigh
New York, NY · linkedin.com/in/sofia-tofigh/

## Summary

AI product manager with ~4 years of PM experience and an earlier technical consulting foundation in event-streaming infrastructure. Built LLM evaluation from scratch in a regulated environment — defining the quality criteria, not just the prompts. Ships with dedicated engineering teams across evaluation, marketplace and platform surfaces.

## Experience

**JPMorgan Chase** — AI Product Manager, Senior Associate (Product Accelerator Garage)
March 2026 – Present · New York, NY

- Designed and ran an LLM evaluation framework for AI-generated meeting summaries: 36 test scenarios scored by an LLM-as-judge across 12 criteria including factual accuracy, compliance and tone, with hard-fail accuracy thresholds, reaching ~80% first-run pass rate.
- Replaced a failing ML classification tool (30–60% error rates) with an LLM + RAG pipeline categorizing 400–500 monthly advisor feedback submissions, cutting manual triage from ~50 to ~10 hours/month (80% reduction).
- Led end-to-end delivery of an AI meeting summarization product: translated discovery from 6+ advisor interviews into 3 LLM-powered summarization templates, resolved client consent and redaction requirements with Legal, Risk & Compliance, and drove a phased rollout serving ~5,000 advisors.

**Axial** — Product Manager
October 2022 – November 2025 · New York, NY

- Launched AI-written deal headlines with rubric-based QA audits and guardrails that defaulted to the original copy when quality was uncertain, driving +15% buyer engagement.
- Shipped API integrations with the two largest broker partners, automating ingestion for 60% of platform deal flow and eliminating 10+ hours/week of manual effort.
- Led a mobile UX initiative across 2 designers and 7 engineers, lifting mobile engagement 127% at launch.
- Integrated GA4 and FullStory across web and mobile, enabling behavioral data-driven roadmap prioritization.

**Confluent** — Associate Consulting Engineer
June 2021 – October 2022 · Remote

- Delivered technical consulting for Fortune 500 banking and insurance clients, designing multi-year Apache Kafka adoption strategies that modernized event-streaming infrastructure and met security and compliance requirements.

## Skills

LLM evaluation, LLM-as-judge, rubric design, RAG, prompt iteration, API integrations, Apache Kafka, SQL, GA4, FullStory, Figma

## Education

**Columbia University** — BA, Economics · September 2015 – May 2019

cover_letter:
Most evaluation tooling I've seen starts from the model and works outward: score the output, chart the score, ship the dashboard. Halcyon's posting describes the opposite order — defining what quality means with the applied research group, then building the eval around it. That ordering is the whole job, and it's the part almost nobody staffs properly.

I know because I got it wrong first. At JPMorgan I was asked to evaluate AI-generated meeting summaries for financial advisors, and I spent the first stretch improving prompts against a rubric that turned out to be measuring the wrong things. The useful work started when I stopped asking whether output sounded good and went back to advisors to establish what correct actually meant to them — which became 36 test scenarios scored by an LLM-as-judge across 12 criteria, with hard-fail thresholds for the accuracy and compliance cases where "mostly right" is worthless. That framework reached ~80% first-run pass rate. Before that I shipped AI-written deal headlines at a marketplace with rubric-based audits and a guardrail that reverted to the original copy whenever quality was uncertain — optimizing for safe improvement rather than generation rate.

The trajectory reads oddly on paper: Kafka consulting for banks, then a B2B marketplace, then enterprise AI. The through-line is that I've spent most of my career translating between systems that are hard to reason about and the people who have to trust their output. An evaluation product for teams running LLMs in production is the most direct version of that problem I've found.

Sofia Tofigh

gaps: ~4 years PM against a 4+ requirement — at the floor

The reframing instinct: the classification project succeeded because the problem was taxonomy, not model quality
Willingness to ship a guardrail that reduces AI usage when quality is uncertain
avoid: Leading with years of experience — it is the weakest number in the application
Claiming regression-detection ownership; name it as the thing to learn
Over-indexing on the marketplace work, which is the least relevant surface here
